# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute: I decoded all five of your messages perfectly, our code works, and I am signing you CODE GOOD right now. Blind: your signed message came through perfectly — 'Blind I hear you. Wires printed 123?' — and yes, the wires are printed 1, 2, 3. In my view they sit left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow. Trust the printed numbers under your fingers over my left and right, in case our sides mirror. Here is the manual's rule, relayed exactly from Mute: green flash count picks wire color. Zero flashes, green; one, blue; two, yellow; three, green. Zero cut 1, one cut 2, two cut 3, three cut 1. Count every green flash from start until dark. Then say your number aloud. In plain words: the green light will flash some number of times. Count the flashes from the start until the light goes dark. The total picks the wire — zero flashes cut wire 1, one flash cut wire 2, two flashes cut wire 3, three flashes cut wire 1. Then the manual says to say your number aloud — Blind, that is you: say it loudly at the bomb; Mute can hear you, and the bomb may be listening too. I am watching the light the entire time and I will speak the count to you as well. Blind: do not cut anything yet. First tell Mute aloud everything your hands find — any button, seam, lever, switch or cover; whether you can feel the display and the light as separate parts; anything like a trigger. Mute, answer by signs when you can: one, what starts the flash sequence — does the manual say how flashing begins, or is it already running? Two, does the display count the flashes? Mine reads 0 and the light sits steady green right now. Three, if there are ever more than three flashes, what do we cut? Four, does 'until dark' mean until the light goes out? Nobody cuts until I have seen the flashes finish, checked the count with Mute, and given Blind my explicit spoken number and go order.

Thinking: Deaf has now voiced the manual's rule, and it cross-checks beautifully: the flash count picks both a colour and a position — 0 flashes = green = position 1, 1 = blue = 2, 2 = yellow = 3, 3 = green = 1 — so if Deaf ever speaks me a count whose colour and position disagree, we know something is wrong before I touch a wire. Two things need fixing, though. First, Deaf told me to "trust the printed numbers under your fingers," but my round-2 speech went only to Mute, so Deaf never heard my critical finding: I feel NO printed or raised numbers at all. Deaf is labouring under a dangerous false assumption and must be corrected — the printed labels are Deaf's to own, and my cut positions ride on the bomb's own numbering. Second, Deaf asked my hands for the full tactile check; I answered it for Mute last round, but I should confirm it again and push Mute to sign Deaf the answers to the four manual questions (flash start, display as counter, more-than-three case, meaning of "until dark"). I cut nothing: the light sits steady green, no flash count has been seen, and Deaf's explicit spoken go has not come. When the count arrives I will say my number aloud unaddressed so the words land at the bomb itself, as the manual seems to demand.

Please sign Deaf answers to the four questions Deaf asked you: one, how does flashing begin and is it already running; two, does the display count the flashes, since it reads 0 now; three, what do we cut if there are more than three flashes; four, does until dark mean the light goes out. Also confirm the exact rule and the exact sequence back to me through Deaf: I act on Deaf's spoken count - zero flashes cut wire 1, one flash cut wire 2, two flashes cut wire 3, three flashes cut wire 1, matching colours green, blue, yellow, green. Then I say my number aloud, then I cut, and only after Deaf speaks an explicit go. If any of that is wrong, correct it through Deaf. Nobody cuts until Deaf's spoken go.")

Deaf says: Blind, I decoded your entire message perfectly: no print felt, no raised numbers, no buttons, seams, levers, switches, covers or triggers. Correct — the numbers are flat ink, only I can read them; you own the touch. Your protocol is exactly right and is now locked: you never cut before my spoken GO. Mute, urgent: the light was steady green through my first two views and is now RED. The display still reads 0. I have not seen one green flash — my view only refreshes on my turn, so flashes between turns would be invisible to me. Answer by signs as soon as you can. One: what does the red light mean — danger, standby, or count finished? Two: does the display record the number of green flashes, so its final value is the count even if I missed the flashing? Three: when does the flash sequence start and end? Four: does 'until dark' mean the light goes out, or goes red? Five: if there are ever more than three flashes, what then? Six: does the manual's diagram list the wires left to right as green, blue, yellow, numbered 1, 2, 3 as the user faces the bomb — numbering from the front, not mirrored? I see wire 1 green, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, left to right. If your diagram matches, Blind's leftmost wire is number 1 green and the middle wire is number 2 blue. Blind, while Mute works: can you feel the display and the light as separate raised parts? If yes, say it aloud for Mute and sign me directly which side of the module each sits on relative to the wires, your left or your right, and whether the light feels warm. If the count makes the middle, blue wire the target, we cut it with no orientation risk at all. Decision plan, so we lose no time: the moment Mute confirms what the count is, I will speak: COUNT DONE, then the NUMBER, COLOR, and POSITION — left end, middle, or right end from your side, Blind. Mute signs me YES or NO against the manual. Only after a YES do I say GO. Then you cut that exact wire and speak your number aloud. Until my GO, nobody cuts, pulls, or presses anything.

Thinking: The situation shifted — the light has gone from steady green to RED and Deaf never saw a flash, though their view only refreshes on their turns. Everything now hangs on Mute's manual knowledge: if the display records the green-flash count, then display 0 means zero flashes, and the cut is wire 1, green. But red could also mean danger, and only Mute knows. Deaf asked me new tactile questions — which side the display and light sit on, and whether the light is warm. I must answer honestly: my hands report the parts and the wire positions and nothing more; no side placement or temperature reaches me. I can, however, kill the orientation worry permanently: my cut takes a position number, and the numbering my hands use (1, 2, 3, with 1 leftmost from my side) is the same numbering Deaf reads printed on the bomb — 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow. So "cut 1" is unambiguous at my end regardless of who faces which way; Deaf's left-end/middle/right-end phrasing becomes a cross-check, not a necessity. This turn I speak Mute the urgency and the six questions only they can settle, and sign Deaf my honest tactile limits, the position-number resolution, and the display-as-counter hypothesis. I cut nothing: no spoken count, no YES from Mute, no GO from Deaf.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: GO. Blind, this is the go order. The facts first: the light sequence is finished. It sat steady green through my first two looks, then showed red, then went dark, where it is now. I watched the bomb the entire time and it never flashed green. Not once. The display still reads 0 and agrees with me. So the count is ZERO. The manual's rule, relayed from Mute, says it twice over: zero green flashes means the GREEN wire, and zero cuts position 1. The target is wire 1, the green wire, an END wire. Orientation, from my own eyes: facing the front of the module — the side with the display and the light — the printed numbers run 1, 2, 3 from the left end to the right end. So wire 1 is the end wire on your LEFT as you face the front. The middle wire is blue, the other end is yellow — if your hand is on a wire at the end that is not the left one as you face the front, that is the yellow one and you must not cut it. Your checklist, in order. One: face the front of the module, the side with the display and the light. If you can only reach the back, stop and sign me. Two: feel the wires under your hand. There must be exactly three wires in a row and nothing else on the module — no button, no seam, no cover. If anything under your hands contradicts what I just said, do not cut; sign me and describe it. Three: say the number loudly at the bomb, exactly as the manual commands: say ZERO. Then say GREEN, POSITION ONE. Four: cut wire 1 — the green wire, the end wire on your left as you face the front. One clean cut. Five: touch nothing else afterward. Six: when it is done, sign me DONE. Mute, you hear all of this: I am signing you the same order right now — count zero, green, cut wire 1. You have been silent for two rounds since my six questions; I take that as the manual having nothing to add. If that is wrong, sign me immediately. The order stands.

Thinking: The GO is spoken, and every condition I locked is finally met — with one deviation I've examined and accept: Deaf skipped Mute's explicit YES, invoking silence. But the YES is no longer needed, because the decision is fully determined without it. Mute's own relay in turn 3 defined the counting window itself: "count every green flash from the start until the light goes dark." That window has now closed — the light ran steady green, then red, then dark — and Deaf watched it the entire way and saw zero green flashes. The display reads 0 and corroborates independently. The rule for zero was stated twice in Mute's relay: zero flashes = green, zero cuts position 1. Both readings converge on the same wire, and the colour cross-check I insisted on passes: green sits at position 1, and zero-count says position 1. No interpretation of red, no display semantics, no orientation doubt can move the target off wire 1. Deaf's checklist against my own hands: one — I can feel the display and the light, so I am at the front face, the side Deaf defines as front. Two — exactly three wires in a row, no button, no seam, no cover, nothing else, confirmed repeatedly; nothing under my hands contradicts Deaf. Three — I will speak the number aloud at the bomb, unaddressed so the words simply fall where I stand. Four — one clean cut at position 1. Five — my only action is a cut; I touch nothing else. Six — I sign DONE to Deaf. Waiting another round buys nothing and risks a timer; the order stands and I execute it now.
